subject: Commercial terms & connector handoff: vector-index translation for tiered storage
messages:
From: Ben Clarke <ben@pinecone.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Sheldon Price <sheldon@atlas-consulting.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: connector approach + commercial outline for tiered vector storage

Hi Marissa / Sergio,

Great to meet last week — thanks for the runway. Quick summary and proposal so we have an auditable starting point before legal redlines. Atlas will be the systems integrator; Pinecone + Weaviate teams will provide support during the integration window. High-level asks:

- Technical: a connector that supports automatic index tiering between fast SSD-backed indexes (Pinecone) and cold object storage (S3) with metadata-preserving rehydration.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for the connector, plus an escalation window for material sync failures.
- Commercial: joint revenue share on managed connector installs for customers (idea to be refined) + a one-time engineering engagement fee to cover SRE/QA.

Attached is a short SOW draft and a strawman SLA (RDW-Pinecone-Connector-SOW-v1.pdf). I'm copying Sheldon from Atlas to align on delivery and estimates.

Next steps: can your team confirm acceptance of the technical scope and provide preferred procurement cadence (PO vs contract)? Happy to schedule a 45-min technical handoff later this week.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Partnerships, Pinecone

Attachments: RDW-Pinecone-Connector-SOW-v1.pdf

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ben Clarke <ben@pinecone.io>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai; dev_patel@redwood.ai; Sheldon Price <sheldon@atlas-consulting.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 12:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: connector approach + commercial outline for tiered vector storage

Ben — thanks for the clear summary and the SOW. High level sign-off from our side on the technical scope; a few clarifying points below before we circle legal/finance: 

1) Connector behavior: we need explicit guarantees about index consistency during partial rehydration (i.e., reads that hit objects pending reindexing). We prefer the connector to present a consistent read model with documented eventual consistency bounds (max staleness = 60s) and observable sync metrics.
2) Data residency: preservation of vector metadata and ability to redact vectors on request (compliance requirement). Confirm S3 object keys will retain provenance tags.
3) Commercial ask: Redwood prefers engineering engagement as a fixed-fee SOW + a 12-month support subscription rather than revenue share for the initial go-to-market; we can revisit revenue share once we have 50+ paid customers onboarded.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical handoff: Wed 2026-06-10 10:00 PT (45 mins) — can we lock this?
- I'll upload a first-pass Connector-SLA-terms-draft.docx for your legal and security teams to review.

Looping Sergio & Dev to coordinate SRE and product acceptance criteria.

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0123

From: Amira Hassan <amira@weaviate.com>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: connector approach + commercial outline for tiered vector storage

Thanks everyone for pulling the handoff together — good session yesterday. A couple of technical clarifications from Weaviate's side we promised to follow up on:

- Rehydration latency targets: Weaviate recommends background rehydration with priority ranking; typical observed rehydrate times for 512-dim embeddings on 1TB indexes is sub-3s when warm cache is available. We'll document microbenchmarks.
- Consistency model: Weaviate can support versioned metadata and will return a 'staleness' header for reads that hit the cold tier. We'll work with Redwood to make that header visible in the API surface.

Commercial notes: we'll accept Redwood's fixed-fee SOW approach. Weaviate proposes a joint launch marketing budget (co-op) — suggested 20k USD for joint webinars, docs, and a technical lab.

Attached: brief performance notes (pasted below) and we will send a short addendum to the SOW if any micro-ops change.

—
Amira Hassan
Partnerships Engineer, Weaviate

Attachments referenced: performance-notes-embed.pdf (sent separately)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Ben Clarke <ben@pinecone.io>; Amira Hassan <amira@weaviate.com>; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai; dev_patel@redwood.ai; Sheldon Price <sheldon@atlas-consulting.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: connector approach + commercial outline for tiered vector storage

Team — quick update from legal/finance after reviewing the SOW and SLA draft. Key points and action items: 

- Legal redlines: remove blanket indemnity for connector noncompliance; instead require joint incident response playbook and limitation of liability aligned with existing Redwood partner terms.
- SLA: agree to 99.9% uptime for connector orchestration; add an operational metric for "sync success rate" (target 99.5% over rolling 30 days).
- Procurement: Redwood will proceed via PO for the fixed-fee engineering engagement (SOW value: USD 85,000). We'll issue a PO once SOW v1 is finalized.
- Marketing co-op: approved at USD 15,000 (counter to Weaviate's 20k ask) — propose we split the delta in a tri-party launch budget.

Action items:
1) Marissa: share SLA redline (I attached Connector-SLA-terms-draft.docx) — please focus on incident playbook language and measurable sync metrics.
2) Ben/Amira/Sheldon: confirm fine with PO procurement and the SOW value.
3) Dev/Product: prepare acceptance test plan for rehydration behavior (include staleness header exposure and automated regression tests).

If we can get confirmations this week we'll route to finance and issue the PO early next week.

Thanks — Laura
Head of Partnerships Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
